To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cell growth and differentiation are controlled by mechanical forces and that the mechanical properties of cells and tissues are controlled by the actin cytoskeleton.
cell shape, cell adhesion, and mechanical tension are all critical for control of cell proliferation and differentiation.

(1) Mechanical forces generated by cells in tissues control the expression of genes responsible for cell proliferation and differentiation, (2) Mechanical forces generated in response to changes in the extracellular microenvironment control cell proliferation and differentiation in a manner that ensures the formation of tissues with the correct shape and size, (3) Mechanical forces generated as a result of changes in cell shape control the expression of growth and differentiation genes to ensure that cells in tissues maintain a balance between cell proliferation and differentiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the physical and biochemical cues that control growth and differentiation of cells in the developing embryo and how these processes are disrupted in cancer.
the role of mechanical cues in cell fate determination and tissue formation.
how cells sense and respond to their physical microenvironment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanical properties of the cytoskeletal network, which is the major determinant of the cell shape, are responsible for the regulation of cell fate.
the mechanical tension-dependent changes are the most critical factor for the cell fate switching.
cell shape is the key regulator of cell proliferation, and the cell shape is determined by the cytoskeletal structure and its mechanical properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mechanical tension-dependent remodeling of the cytoskeleton and cell shape are critical for cell fate switching and growth control.
the cell shape and the cytoskeletal structure play important roles in cell fate decision.
the cytoskeleton is the key to cell fate decisions and that cell shape is a major determinant of the cytoskeletal structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cells use mechanical forces to control cell proliferation and fate switching, and that these processes are controlled by a common mechanism that involves the actin cytoskeleton.
cells use a combination of biochemical and biophysical cues to sense the local environment and to respond to it in a coordinated manner.
cells are not simply passive responders to external cues.
